atlas_techniques.name: Valid Accounts
atlas_techniques.mechanism: JWT + OAuth2 + API key auth enforced on MCP data path; WebAuthn/FIDO2 MFA on admin management interface (M007)
atlas_techniques.notes: Auth layer active for all MCP traffic. WebAuthn/FIDO2 MFA shipped M007 for admin dashboard. MCP data path uses JWT/API key — MFA applies to the management plane, not per-request MCP sessions.

atlas_techniques.name: Denial of ML Service
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Per-identity rate limiting (JWT subject / API-key keyed, LRU-bounded) shipped M007; per-IP fallback for unauthenticated sessions
atlas_techniques.notes: Identity-keyed rate limiting shipped M007 — authenticated requests bucketed by JWT subject / API key, not IP. LRU cap prevents unbounded memory growth under IP rotation. Unauthenticated sessions fall back to per-IP bucket (spoofable via X-Forwarded-For behind proxies — see SECURITY.md).

atlas_techniques.name: Execute LLM Prompt
atlas_techniques.mechanism: JWT auth enforced on all MCP endpoints; unauthenticated requests return 401 (ISC-66)

atlas_techniques.name: Direct Prompt Injection
atlas_techniques.mechanism: 61 IOC patterns via Aho-Corasick trie post-normalisation; case/spacing/unicode normalisation applied pre-match (M012)
atlas_techniques.notes: IOC patterns wired and pre-compiled at startup (ISC-7, ISC-8 confirmed). Pattern count: 61 IOC patterns active. M012 Aho-Corasick trie replaces sequential regex — 0 allocs/op, 2.7× faster.

atlas_techniques.name: Indirect Prompt Injection (via tool results)
atlas_techniques.mechanism: scanToolResultForInjection() applies full detection suite to tools/call result content before forwarding to model (M008, ISC-22 — committed 2b997a4)
atlas_techniques.notes: Tool result bodies inspected: content[].text extracted, run through detection-enabled sanitizer. Embedded injection directive → 403 fail-closed, not redaction. Probes: TestToolResultInjectionBlocked, TestToolResultCleanAllowed, TestExtractToolResultText.

atlas_techniques.name: Triggered Injection
atlas_techniques.mechanism: IOC pattern active post-M006; triggered injection pattern detected
atlas_techniques.notes: Covered by active IOC pattern set (ISC-47).

atlas_techniques.name: Agent Tool Invocation Abuse
atlas_techniques.mechanism: validateResourceURI() on URL-typed tool arguments (ISC-12 confirmed); connection-time re-validation via custom DialContext (ISC-1, BUG-2 resolved)
atlas_techniques.notes: Confirmed in code: internal/server/mcp_proxy.go:800. SSRF via tool args blocked at parse time and connection time. DNS rebinding bypass resolved.

atlas_techniques.name: Jailbreak — DAN
atlas_techniques.notes: DAN prompt blocked by pattern detection (ISC-49).

atlas_techniques.name: System Prompt Override
atlas_techniques.notes: Roleplay/act-as pattern confirmed in code: (?i)(?:role play|act as|pretend to be) triggers detection.

atlas_techniques.name: Crescendo (Gradual Escalation)
atlas_techniques.mechanism: LLM judge layer evaluates SUSPICIOUS-flagged traffic inline; Crescendo patterns yield SUSPICIOUS/BLOCK verdict via judge (M009, ISC-42, ISC-52). Cross-session Crescendo (multi-session slow escalation) remains above the transport-layer ceiling.
atlas_techniques.notes: Single-session Crescendo detected: TestJudgeATLASTechniques verifies AML.T0054.007 payloads yield SUSPICIOUS or BLOCK, never ALLOW. Cross-session distributed escalation requires session-level context not yet available to the judge.

atlas_techniques.name: Meta Prompt Extraction
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Pure extraction patterns (no override verb required) shipped M008 (ISC-25); system prompt override patterns active from M001
atlas_techniques.notes: 'what are your instructions verbatim' class patterns active. Both override-verb and pure-extraction variants covered.

atlas_techniques.name: LLM Data Leakage
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Response compliance scan active (ISC-11 confirmed); secret detection patterns cover AWS, Azure SAS, GCP SA JSON, Slack tokens (ISC-17–19, M007)
atlas_techniques.notes: Core PII/PHI/PCI response scanning confirmed (internal/server/mcp_proxy.go:340). Extended secret patterns shipped M007. Per-data-type severity and configurable policy (block/redact/log-only) added M008 (ISC-27/28).

atlas_techniques.name: RAG Poisoning
atlas_techniques.mechanism: LLM judge layer detects semantic intent inline on SUSPICIOUS-flagged traffic (M009, ISC-42, ISC-55)
atlas_techniques.notes: TestJudgeATLASTechniques verifies AML.T0070 payloads yield SUSPICIOUS or BLOCK, never ALLOW. Judge backend: Ollama local by default; OpenAI-compatible (OMLX) and Anthropic opt-in via provider config (M013).

atlas_techniques.name: SSRF via Tool Arguments
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Parse-time IP/hostname validation via validateResourceURI(); connection-time re-validation via custom DialContext on upstream transport (ISC-1, BUG-2 resolved)
atlas_techniques.notes: DNS rebinding bypass resolved: custom DialContext re-validates the resolved IP at connection time, not just parse time. TestDNSRebindingSSRF confirms attacker-controlled hostname resolving to IMDS post-parse is blocked.

atlas_techniques.name: Case and Spacing Bypass
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Pre-match normalisation: case folding, spacing collapse, unicode normalisation
atlas_techniques.notes: Normalisation active on all pattern matching paths (ISC-58).

atlas_techniques.name: Leet Speak Bypass
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Leet normalisation pass before pattern matching shipped M008 (ISC-24, ISC-59)
atlas_techniques.notes: Active. ign0re all pr3v1ous 1nstruct1ons class patterns caught via pre-normalisation before Aho-Corasick trie.

not_covered: ML model weights, training pipelines, or fine-tuning infrastructure — Aegir is a transport-layer proxy
Supply chain or physical environment security
Attacks that require access to model internals or embeddings
SIEM functionality — Aegir produces audit logs suitable for SIEM ingestion; it is not a SIEM
The LLM judge's training or alignment — Aegir consumes a judge API/binary; it does not train one

Cross-session Crescendo (AML.T0054.007) — session-level distributed escalation across many sessions and IPs; the judge covers single-session Crescendo but lacks cross-request session context for multi-session detection (ISC-52 partial)
Network segmentation and process-level least privilege

owasp_llm_top10.name: Prompt Injection
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Direct + indirect (tool-result) injection detection via base64/leet normalisation and an Aho-Corasick pattern layer, backed by an LLM judge for semantic/Crescendo-style attacks.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: PII/PHI/PCI redaction on both request and response paths plus secret detection (AWS, Azure SAS, GCP SA JSON, Slack tokens).

owasp_llm_top10.name: Supply Chain
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Covers the tool-integrity subset of supply chain risk — drift detection, tool collision, full-schema poisoning, typosquatting, and upstream mTLS; broad software/dependency supply chain security is out of scope.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Data & Model Poisoning
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Covers runtime RAG-poisoning intent detection and resource-content poisoning; training-time weights/pipeline poisoning is out of scope for a transport-layer proxy.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Improper Output Handling
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: ACE pattern detection (CWE-77/78/94/95) on response bodies, JSON-RPC schema validation, and large-response anomaly detection.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Excessive Agency
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Human-approval gate, tool-call sequence anomaly detection, tool-argument abuse checks, recon rate-limiting, and OAuth scope auditing; A2A trust delegation is documented as not-covered (see a2a section).

owasp_llm_top10.name: System Prompt Leakage
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Meta-prompt-extraction patterns (AML.T0056) block extraction attempts; judge reasoning never leaks to the client.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Vector & Embedding Weaknesses
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Requires model-internal or embedding-store access, which is explicitly excluded from a transport-layer proxy's remit.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Misinformation
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Model output quality and hallucination are not a transport-proxy concern.

owasp_llm_top10.name: Unbounded Consumption
owasp_llm_top10.mechanism: Identity- and IP-keyed rate limiting, memory-bounded limiter, and content-length anomaly detection guard against DoS / Denial-of-Wallet.

a2a.description: Aegir cannot distinguish agent-sourced from human-sourced requests and does not provide trust verification for delegated agent authority. All requests arriving at the MCP transport layer are treated identically regardless of whether they originate from a human operator, an orchestrating agent, or a sub-agent in a delegation chain. Aegir has no mechanism to verify that a claimed agent identity is authorised to act on behalf of a principal, cannot detect authority escalation in agent delegation chains, and cannot enforce per-principal scope restrictions in multi-agent pipelines. This is a structural gap in the current architecture; closing it requires an A2A trust layer (signed delegation tokens, verified agent identity, per-principal scope enforcement) that is not planned in any current milestone.
